perspective:
Harold’s available information:

- He is Harold Padilla, a project manager, currently responsible for a project whose progress is worrying him.
- He perceives his team as unmotivated and feels frustrated, anxious, and at his wit’s end.
- He knows Arthur as a trusted friend/advisor and arranged a coffee-shop meeting with him to seek advice.
- He heard Arthur suggest understanding each team member’s individual motivations and having one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood.
- He admitted to Arthur that he had been focused mainly on goals and deadlines, decided to try Arthur’s advice, and felt more hopeful/relieved afterward.
- He told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to learn what motivates each of them. He heard TM1 say this could be helpful and TM2 say they were open to it. He planned to schedule those chats and said they should make the project a success together.
- Later, he observed that the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding. Arthur told him there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that he might need to dig deeper. Harold decided to set up another round of meetings.
- In those meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns. He heard TM1 say there was tension among a few team members affecting work. He heard TM2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and try to redistribute tasks to ease pressure. He told TM2 their well-being was important to him.
- Harold decided to create a more supportive, open team environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He told the team about this plan. He heard TM1 say it sounded great and would help, and TM2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said their input and well-being were crucial and urged everyone to work together for project success.
